summary: Build a simple romantic interactive Valentine web page (HTML/CSS/JS) for iPad Chrome with Yes/No choices, evasive No button, and a simple text message shown after Yes (instead of a meme image).
architectural_notes: Implement as a self-contained HTML/CSS/JS page optimized for iPad Chrome touch/hover behavior.

existing_features.title: Create a single-purpose Valentine proposal page that asks the question “Will you be my Valentine?” and presents exactly two options: “Yes” and “No”, using a romantic pink-and-white theme.

Make the “No” option evade interaction: when the user hovers or points at “No” (mouse/trackpad) or attempts to tap it (touch), the “No” button should reposition within the visible viewport so it cannot be clicked.
When the user clicks “Yes”, replace the question/options view with a result view that displays a meme image containing the text: “Found me jiyuu ❤️ , By the way good choice 😘”.
Add the required generated meme image to the frontend as a static asset under frontend/public/assets/generated and render it directly from the frontend (do not fetch it via the backend).

Update the post-Yes result view so that after the user clicks “Yes”, the app shows a simple text-only message using the previously mentioned wording (“Found me jiyuu ❤️ , By the way good choice 😘”) and does not display the meme image.

new_feature_requests.summary: Create a single-purpose romantic Valentine web page (pink/white theme) asking 'Will you be my Valentine?' runnable in Chrome on iPad
Add Yes/No options where the No button moves away on hover to prevent clicking
After clicking Yes, show a simple text message (use the previously mentioned wording) instead of displaying a meme image

projectName: Romantic Valentine single-page interaction with evasive No button and Yes reveal meme
